description: N5/C2 privacy finding triage: which residual leak vector remains

residual_vector.instructions: In this design, which single residual vector is the most plausible way sensitive healthcare information still reaches or is inferable from a stored activity record?

criteria.caller_supplied_reference: Opaque reference fields are minted by the calling source, so an identifier that embeds a name, phone number, national id or medical record number can be stored even though it has no spaces
criteria.read_time_join: The read surface derives a title from enumerations and could join the subject reference to clinical data, exposing clinical detail outside the activity row itself
criteria.metadata_inference: Even with codes only, an operations reader can infer a clinically sensitive fact from branch, actor, category and timing correlated with an identified patient
criteria.guessable_reference: Reference tokens are not unguessable, so activity rows can be enumerated to learn which subjects have activity
criteria.other: None of the above; the residual risk lies elsewhere

no_direct_identifier.instructions: The design refuses a direct patient identifier (name, phone number, national id, email, medical record number) that is smuggled in as a reference-shaped token with no spaces

criteria.true: A pattern or registry control refuses reference tokens that are direct identifiers even when they contain no whitespace
criteria.false: A direct identifier with no whitespace passes every stated control

metadata_only_disclosure.instructions: The design's disclosure is limited to the fact that an operational, non-clinical event occurred; the design does not let activity describe a clinical finding, result value, medication, diagnosis or note

criteria.true: The closed source registry and severity registry admit only operational, non-clinical events, so no clinical finding is expressible
criteria.false: A clinical finding, result value, medication, diagnosis or note can be expressed or inferred from a record
